title: Dallas Fed Texas Service Sector Outlook Survey (Nov 2026 data)
source: EST: dallasfed.org's Texas Service Sector Outlook Survey page, fetched direct 2026-09-05 (HTTP 200, desktop user-agent) — its '2026 release dates' table carries the column header `Release (9:30 a.m. CT)` and the row `November | Tuesday, Dec. 1`, alongside the note that 'The publishing process begins at 9:30 a.m. CT' and that Dallas 'cannot guarantee the exact timing all survey content becomes available online'. 9:30 a.m. CT = 10:30 ET. Consistent with the survey's observed one-business-day lag behind the Texas Manufacturing Outlook Survey on the same page (Jan 27, Feb 24, Mar 31, Apr 28, May 27, Jun 30, Jul 28, Sep 1, Sep 29, Oct 27, Dec 1, Dec 29 against manufacturing's Jan 26 … Nov 30, Dec 28). Filed estimate on three counts: the publisher's availability is demonstrably intermittent (the same site returned HTTP 403 to the 2026-09-01 session and 200 today), this lane never self-promotes an adjacency it discovered in-sweep, and — the binding one — the source-prefix table in market-events-data.ts has no confirmed tier for a reserve-bank survey page at all (`FED:` is scoped to federalreserve.gov's FOMC calendar), so no source quality can promote this entry. The 10:30 ET time is a process start, not a guaranteed release instant
notes: The services half of the Dallas Fed's Texas survey pair, and the reason to file it now: it is the only Texas services read, and this cycle's inflation stickiness is a services story, not a goods one. It lands 10:30 ET on 2026-12-01, one business day after dallas-fed-mfg-2026-11-30 and 30 minutes after both ISM Manufacturing (ism-manufacturing-2026-12-01) and JOLTS (jolts-2026-12-01) — so on that morning it is the third macro release inside 30 minutes and its own footprint is unmeasurable, which is exactly why it is filed `low` rather than `medium`. The dallas-fed-mfg-2026-09-28 research declined to file this survey on 2026-09-01 for one stated reason only — 'its 2026 schedule could not be established from any fetchable source (dallasfed.org 403; search results were self-contradictory)'. That reason is now retired: the schedule is quoted verbatim from the publisher's own table. Discovered during the dallas-fed-mfg-2026-11-30 initial-research adjacency sweep (2026-09-05). Two facts added by this entry's own initial research (2026-09-05, docs/research/events/dallas-fed-tssos-2026-12-01.md): (1) the pair shares ONE field window — both August reports read verbatim 'collected August 18–26', as do Nov-25 'Nov. 10–18', Jan-26 'Jan. 13–21', Jun-26 'June 16–24' and Jul-26 'July 14–22' — so this print carries no observation collected after dallas-fed-mfg-2026-11-30's, and the two headline indexes correlate r=+0.893 over 235 common months (though only r²=0.466 on 2023–2026, which is why the entry is still worth reading); (2) a composition break — the Texas Retail Outlook Survey was discontinued from the January 2026 release and retail folded into this survey, and the August 2026 release also carried the annual seasonal-factor revision, so pre-2026 history is not the same instrument and any base rate must be recomputed on a freshly downloaded vintage.
